statement: A continuous noncuspidal section of a smooth hyperbolic curve over Q whose localizations are ordinary or cuspidal and ordinary integral outside a finite set is a rational point section if a nonconstant unit is regular and nonzero at all its local cusp centres. A finite étale neighbourhood with unit rank greater than the number of cuspidal finite places supplies such a unit, conditionally on its existence. For the tripod, cofinite ordinary integrality and at most one local cusp label suffice; in particular D.30 finite ramification plus this label restriction implies a rational point section.

notes: Root independently approved the complete unit and single-label proofs. Arbitrary completed tangential classes are included because regular nonzero units are unramified along the horizontal cusp. The neighbourhood unit-rank inequality is a hypothesis, not an existence theorem. Harari-Voloch Theorem1 is used only for the outside-S closure/descent comparison; its Conjecture2 is not asserted proved. Helm-Voloch and Liu-Xu retain their exact omitted-place and finite-set hypotheses. The mixed-label case and finite ramification for arbitrary sections remain unresolved. D1-D4 are not promoted.
